source.text: Πάλιν μοι λέγει· Ἀλήθειαν ἀγάπα, καὶ πᾶσα ἀλήθεια ἐκ τοῦ στόματός σου ἐκπορευέσθω, ἵνα τὸ πνεῦμα, ὃ ὁ Θεὸς κατῴκισεν ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ ταύτῃ, ἀληθὲς εὑρεθῇ παρὰ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις, καὶ οὕτως δοξασθήσεται ὁ Κύριος ὁ ἐν σοὶ κατοικῶν· ὅτι ὁ Κύριος ἀληθινὸς ἐν παντὶ ῥήματι, καὶ οὐδὲν παρ’ αὐτῷ ψεῦδος· 2. οἱ οὖν ψευδόμενοι ἀθετοῦσι τὸν Κύριον καὶ γίνονται ἀποστερηταὶ τοῦ Κυρίου, μὴ παραδιδόντες αὐτῷ τὴν παρακαταθήκην ἣν ἔλαβον. ἔλαβον γὰρ παρ’ αὐτοῦ πνεῦμα ἄψευστον. τοῦτο ἐὰν ψευδὲς ἀποδώσωσιν, ἐμίαναν τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀποστερηταί. 3. ταῦτα οὖν ἀκούσας ἐγὼ ἔκλαυσα λίαν. ἰδὼν δέ με κλαίοντα λέγει· Τί κλαίεις; Ὅτι, φημί, κύριε, οὐκ οἶδα εἰ δύναμαι σωθῆναι. Διατί; φησίν. Οὐδέπω γάρ, φημί, κύριε, ἐν τῇ ἐμῇ ζωῇ ἀληθὲς ἐλάλησα ῥῆμα, ἀλλὰ πάντοτε πανοῦργος ἔζησα μετὰ πάντων, καὶ τὸ ψεῦδός μου ἀληθὲς ἐπέδειξα παρὰ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις· καὶ οὐδέποτέ μοι οὐδεὶς ἀντεῖπεν, ἀλλ’ ἐπιστεύθη τῷ λόγῳ μου. πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, δύναμαι ζῆσαι ταῦτα πράξας; 4. Σὺ μέν, φησί, καλῶς καὶ ἀληθῶς φρονεῖς· ἔδει γάρ σε ὡς Θεοῦ δοῦλον ἐν ἀληθείᾳ πορεύεσθαι καὶ πονηρὰν συνείδησιν μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ἀληθείας μὴ κατοικεῖν, μηδὲ λύπην ἐπάγειν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ σεμνῷ καὶ ἀληθεῖ. Οὐδέποτε, φημί, κύριε, τοιαῦτα ῥήματα ἀκριβῶς ἤκουσα. 5. Νῦν οὖν, φησίν, ἀκούεις· φύλασσε αὐτά, ἵνα καὶ τὰ πρότερον ἃ ἐλάλησας ψεύδη ἐν ταῖς πραγματείαις σου, τούτων εὑρεθέντων ἀληθινῶν, κἀκεῖνα πιστὰ γένηται· δύναται γὰρ κἀκεῖνα πιστὰ γενέσθαι. ἐὰν ταῦτα φυλάξῃς καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν πᾶσαν ἀλήθειαν λαλήσῃς, δυνήσῃ σεαυτῷ ζωὴν περιποιήσασθαι. καὶ ὃς ἂν ἀκούσῃ τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην καὶ ἀπέχηται τοῦ πονηροτάτου ψεύσματος, ζήσεται τῷ Θεῷ.

translation.text:
Again he says to me: “Love truth[a], and let all truth go forth from your mouth, so that the spirit which God has caused to dwell in this flesh may be found true before all people, and thus the Lord who dwells in you will be glorified; for the Lord is true in every word, and there is no falsehood with him.

Therefore those who lie reject the Lord and become defrauders of the Lord, not handing back to him the deposit that they received. For they received from him a spirit without falsehood. If they return it false, they have defiled the command of the Lord and have become defrauders.

So when I heard these things, I wept greatly. But seeing me weeping, he says, ‘Why are you weeping?’ ‘Because, sir,’ I say, ‘I do not know whether I can be saved.’ ‘Why?’ he says. ‘For,’ I say, ‘sir, never yet in my life have I spoken a true word, but I have always lived deceitfully with everyone, and I made my lie appear true before all people; and no one ever contradicted me, but my word was believed. How then,’ I say, ‘sir, can I live, having done these things?’

He says, ‘You are thinking rightly and truly; for it was necessary for you, as a servant of God, to walk in truth, and not to let an evil conscience dwell with the spirit of truth[b], nor to bring grief upon the holy and true Spirit.’ ‘Never,’ I say, ‘sir, have I heard such words clearly.’

‘Now then,’ he says, ‘you are hearing; keep them, so that even the former lies that you spoke in your dealings, if these are found true, those also may become credible; for those too can become credible. If you keep these and from now on speak all truth, you will be able to gain life for yourself[g][f][e][d][c]. And whoever hears this command and abstains from the most evil lie will live to God.’

footnotes.text: ‘Defrauders’ translates ἀποστερηταί, active ‘those who deprive/defraud.’ Some take it as ‘bereft of the Lord,’ but the deposit image favors the active sense.
‘Deposit’ (παρακαταθήκη) is a technical term for something entrusted for safekeeping; compare 1 Timothy 6:20; 2 Timothy 1:12, 14.
‘Venerable’ renders σεμνός; alternatives include ‘august’ or ‘noble.’ The word is not the usual term for ‘holy’ (ἅγιος).
‘When these are found true’ (τούτων εὑρεθέντων ἀληθινῶν) may refer either to the words now spoken truly (preferred) or to the former utterances themselves.
‘Sir’ translates κύριε in direct address to the messenger, to distinguish from ‘the Lord’ (Κύριος) used of God/the Lord in the same unit.
‘Will live to God’ renders the Greek dative; ‘will live for God’ is a smoother alternative.

theological_decisions.issue: Identity of the spirit given by God and dwelling “in this flesh” (πνεῦμα … κατῴκισεν ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ ταύτῃ)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: The spirit is the divine gift from God (often associated with the holy spirit in early Christian idiom), characterized as ‘without falsehood,’ dwelling in the believer.
alternative_readings: The human spirit/breath created by God.
theological_decisions.rationale: The parallel statements—receiving from God ‘a spirit without falsehood,’ returning it ‘false,’ and glorifying ‘the Lord who dwells in you’—favor a divine indwelling gift rather than merely human psyche or breath.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Active: ‘defrauders of the Lord’—they wrong the Lord by failing to return the entrusted deposit.
alternative_readings: Passive: ‘bereft of the Lord’ (i.e., deprived of the Lord).
theological_decisions.rationale: Lexically ἀποστερητής is an active agent (‘defrauder, depriver’). The deposit metaphor (‘not handing back the deposit’) confirms the active sense.

theological_decisions.issue: Referent of ‘these’ in ‘when these are found true’ (τούτων εὑρεθέντων ἀληθινῶν)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: ‘These’ refers to the words now spoken truly; as these are found true, former words (once lies) may become trusted as your reputation is restored.
alternative_readings: ‘These’ refers back to the former utterances themselves, paradoxically ‘found true.’
theological_decisions.rationale: The logic of restored credibility fits the admonition: present truthfulness rehabilitates one’s word. The alternative creates a paradox less coherent in context.

theological_decisions.issue: Scope of ‘the most wicked lie’ (τοῦ πονηροτάτου ψεύσματος)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: General superlative intensifying all lying rather than a technical reference to perjury or denial of the Lord.
alternative_readings: A specific vice such as perjury; apostasy (denial of the Lord).
theological_decisions.rationale: The immediate context concerns comprehensive truth-telling in speech, not oaths or apostasy. The superlative heightens the moral gravity of lying broadly.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: ‘Slave of God’ in this paraenetic context to preserve the bonded identity and obligation.
theological_decisions.rationale: Project default: use ‘slave’ where the ownership/obligation dimension is salient to the exhortation.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: ‘Will live to God’ preserves the dative orientation.
theological_decisions.rationale: Maintains the textual wording and early-Christian idiom; footnote provides the smoother alternative.

review_passes.summary: The draft is highly accurate and captures Hermas's tone well. A few minor adjustments were made to restore omitted conjunctions and dialogue tags, correct the syntax of an infinitive clause, and improve lexical consistency.
issues_found: Omission of minor connective words and dialogue tags in verse 3: οὖν ('So'), δέ ('But'), and φημί ('I say').

Grammar: In verse 4, πονηρὰν συνείδησιν is the accusative subject of the infinitive κατοικεῖν ('for a wicked conscience not to dwell'), rather than the object of an implied 'have' ('not to have a wicked conscience dwelling').

Awkward English / Over-translation: In verse 4, 'words like this so precisely' expands τοιαῦτα and adds 'so'; 'such words precisely' is closer to τοιαῦτα ῥήματα ἀκριβῶς. In verse 5, 'the former things which you spoke as lies' is clunky for τὰ πρότερον ἃ ἐλάλησας ψεύδη ('the former lies which you spoke').

Lexical consistency: φυλάξῃς in verse 5 was translated 'keep', but the imperative φύλασσε just before was 'guard'. πᾶσα ἀλήθεια was rendered 'every truth' but is better rendered 'all truth' consistently with πᾶσαν ἀλήθειαν later in the unit.

translation.text: So those who lie reject the Lord and cheat him, because they do not return what he entrusted to them as he gave it. They received from him a spirit free from falsehood. If they return that spirit corrupted by lies, they have defiled the Lord’s command and become cheats.

simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Those who lie wrongfully withhold from the Lord what belongs to him.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The common verb “cheat” clearly conveys the force of “defrauders.”

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: not handing back to him the deposit that they received
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: do not return what he entrusted to them as he gave it
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The Lord gave them something in trust that they must return unspoiled.
simplification_decisions.rationale: This keeps the image of an entrusted deposit while avoiding opaque financial language.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: If they return that spirit corrupted by lies
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Lying spoils the originally falsehood-free spirit they received from the Lord.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The recast sentence identifies the pronoun and makes the contrast with a falsehood-free spirit explicit.

interpretive_expansions.rendering: return that spirit corrupted by lies
interpretive_expansions.claim: Their lying corrupts the spirit that was given without falsehood.
evidence: The preceding sentence identifies the received deposit as a spirit without falsehood.
The paragraph directly connects lying with returning the entrusted spirit in a false condition.

risk_flags.mitigation: The surrounding language about an entrusted deposit preserves the serious moral and theological charge.

base_translation.text: So when I heard these things, I wept greatly. But seeing me weeping, he says, ‘Why are you weeping?’ ‘Because, sir,’ I say, ‘I do not know whether I can be saved.’ ‘Why?’ he says. ‘For,’ I say, ‘sir, never yet in my life have I spoken a true word, but I have always lived deceitfully with everyone, and I made my lie appear true before all people; and no one ever contradicted me, but my word was believed. How then,’ I say, ‘sir, can I live, having done these things?’

translation.text:
When I heard this, I wept deeply. He saw me and asked, “Why are you weeping?”

“Because, sir,” I answered, “I do not know whether I can be saved.”

“Why not?” he asked.

“Because, sir, I have never spoken a true word in my whole life. I have always deceived everyone. I made all my lies seem true, and no one ever challenged me; everyone believed what I said. After doing all this, sir, how can I live?”

simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB base text and immediate narrative context
simplification_decisions.rationale: This expresses intense grief without adding a beginning or a particular kind of sorrow.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: I have always lived deceitfully with everyone
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: His whole way of dealing with others was marked by deceit.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The direct verb makes the confession easier to understand.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: no one ever contradicted me, but my word was believed
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: no one ever challenged me; everyone believed what I said
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: His false claims went unopposed and were accepted as true.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB base text and clause contrast
simplification_decisions.rationale: The recast wording keeps both parts of the contrast clear.

risk_flags.risk: “How can I live?” may concern eternal life or salvation rather than merely continuing to exist.
risk_flags.mitigation: The preceding question about salvation preserves the context without resolving the expression.

spob_revision_history.previous_text:
When I heard this, I began to weep bitterly. He saw me and asked, “Why are you weeping?”

“Because, sir,” I answered, “I do not know whether I can be saved.”

“Why not?” he asked.

“Because, sir, I have never spoken a true word in my whole life. I have always deceived everyone. I made all my lies seem true, and no one ever challenged me; everyone believed what I said. After doing all this, sir, how can I live?”
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft substantially improves readability while preserving the confession of pervasive deceit, its acceptance by others, and the unresolved, salvation-contextual force of “How can I live?” No doctrinal expansion is introduced. A small revision is needed because “began to weep bitterly” goes beyond the stated intensity of the POB wording; “I wept deeply” communicates the grief clearly without adding that nuance.

base_translation.text: He says, ‘You are thinking rightly and truly; for it was necessary for you, as a slave of God, to walk in truth, and not to let an evil conscience dwell with the spirit of truth, nor to bring grief upon the holy and true Spirit.’ ‘Never,’ I say, ‘sir, have I heard such words clearly.’

translation.text:
He says, “Your thoughts are right and true. As a servant of God, you must live truthfully. Do not allow an evil conscience to live alongside the spirit of truth, and do not grieve the holy and true Spirit.”

I reply, “Sir, I have never heard words like these so clearly.”

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: You are thinking rightly and truly
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: Your thoughts are right and true
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: His thinking is affirmed as both correct and truthful.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The direct statement is easier to understand than the abstract adverbial wording.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: it was necessary for you, as a slave of God, to walk in truth
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: As a slave of God, you must live truthfully
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Serving God requires a life governed by truth.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Live truthfully” clearly conveys the walking image’s ethical force.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: not to let an evil conscience dwell with the spirit of truth, nor to bring grief upon the holy and true Spirit
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: Do not allow an evil conscience to live alongside the spirit of truth, and do not grieve the holy and true Spirit
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: An evil conscience must not coexist with truth or cause grief to the Spirit.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The two distinct warnings remain intact in ordinary English.

risk_flags.risk: “Live truthfully” no longer displays the source image of walking in truth.
risk_flags.mitigation: It preserves the image’s contextual meaning as a way of life.

risk_flags.risk: The relationship between “spirit of truth” and “holy and true Spirit” remains uncertain.
risk_flags.mitigation: The wording preserves the POB distinction without resolving it.

spob_revision_history.previous_text:
He says, “Your thoughts are right and true. As a slave of God, you must live truthfully. Do not allow an evil conscience to live alongside the spirit of truth, and do not grieve the holy and true Spirit.”

I reply, “Sir, I have never heard words like these expressed so clearly.”
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The revision meaningfully clarifies the POB: “Your thoughts” is direct, “must live truthfully” communicates the ethical force of walking in truth, and the two warnings remain distinct. It also properly retains the textual distinction between “the spirit of truth” and “the holy and true Spirit,” rather than resolving their relationship. Revise only the final clause to avoid adding that the words were “expressed” clearly; retain the source/POB focus on what Hermas heard clearly.

base_translation.text: ‘Now then,’ he says, ‘you are hearing; keep them, so that even the former lies that you spoke in your dealings, if these are found true, those also may become credible; for those too can become credible. If you keep these and from now on speak all truth, you will be able to gain life for yourself. And whoever hears this command and abstains from the most evil lie will live to God.’

translation.text: “Now listen,” he says. “Keep these commands you are hearing, so that even the former lies you told in your dealings—if they are found true—may become believable, for they too can become believable. If you keep these commands and from now on tell the whole truth, you will be able to gain life for yourself. Whoever hears this command and keeps away from the most evil lie will live to God.”

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: Keep these commands you are hearing
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The hearer must obey the commands now being received.
simplification_decisions.rationale: Naming the commands makes the object of “keep” clear without changing its force.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: the former lies that you spoke in your dealings
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: the former lies you told in your dealings
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The statement concerns earlier falsehoods spoken in the hearer’s interactions.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Lies you told” is more natural modern English than “lies that you spoke.”

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: abstains from the most evil lie
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: keeps away from the most evil lie
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The hearer must cease involvement in the condemned falsehood.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Keeps away from” clearly expresses abstaining while preserving the phrase “the most evil lie.”

risk_flags.risk: The claim that former lies may be found true remains logically difficult.
risk_flags.mitigation: The wording preserves the POB’s ambiguity and its purpose connection without explaining it away.

risk_flags.risk: “Live to God” is less idiomatic than “live for God.”
risk_flags.mitigation: The phrase is retained because “for God” could shift the meaning toward service.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: “Now listen,” he says. “Obey what you are hearing. Then, if the former lies you told in your dealings are found to be true, they too may be believed, for they can become believable. If you obey these words and from now on always tell the truth, you will be able to gain life for yourself. Whoever hears this command and turns away from that most evil lie will live for God.”
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft usefully clarifies “keep” as obedience and makes the call to truthful speech natural in modern English. Revision is needed to preserve the POB’s purpose connection, avoid making “the lie” a previously identified specific lie, and retain “live to God” rather than shifting it to the service-oriented “live for God.”
